probe: the kernel hostname and the boot id are readable; os-release may still be honestly missing, which is an absent decline, never a probe failure

collections.name: identity
collections.question: what machine is this, and what operating system is it running?

OsId.sentence: The distribution's machine-readable identifier, identical on every install of the distro.

OsVersionId.sentence: The release this install tracks; rolling distributions genuinely have none, and say so through the absent list rather than a placeholder.

OsPrettyName.sentence: The distribution's own display name for this release, printed as it wrote it.

Hostname.sentence: The kernel hostname, which is also this object's native name: the name observed, never a minted id.

collections.redaction_exemption: every served fact is a single declared scalar; the evidence document is os-release verbatim, whose remaining members are distribution constants that disclose nothing

reference_commands.purpose: the same identity document, by hand
the hostname as the kernel reports it

collections.name: time
collections.question: is this machine's clock synchronised, and through what?

Timezone.sentence: The configured timezone, as timedated states it — a location statement by construction, which is why it is classed as one.

LocalRTC.sentence: Whether the hardware clock is kept in local time rather than UTC — the dual-boot arrangement that makes two systems argue over one RTC.

NTP.sentence: Whether systemd's network time synchronisation is enabled.

NTPSynchronized.sentence: Whether the kernel reports the clock synchronised, whoever synchronised it — true under chrony as much as under timesyncd.

CurrentTime.sentence: The wall clock at acquisition, UTC, seconds precision. A gauge: two correct readings differ by however long passed between them, and a hub compares wall readings across hosts to observe skew (DESIGN 09).

CurrentNTPServer.sentence: The server timesyncd is currently using. Absent where timesyncd has selected none yet, unobservable where timesyncd is not the syncer at all — two different statements, on their own channels.

SystemNTPServers.sentence: The configured server list, which is often an internal name — the reason this whole family is classed as location.

FallbackNTPServers.sentence: The compiled-in fallbacks timesyncd would use with nothing configured.

PollIntervalSeconds.sentence: The [minimum, maximum] polling bounds timesyncd currently applies, rounded to whole seconds from the microsecond pair the interface serves.

rules.sentence: NTP is enabled but the clock is not synchronised.

reference_commands.purpose: the sync source detail, where timesyncd runs
the exact document this collector parses

collections.redaction_exemption: every served fact is a declared scalar or server-name list from the two GetAll replies; the location-classed members (timezone, server names) are declared as such and handled by disclosure policy, and no free-form document is served as evidence

collections.name: overview
collections.question: how loaded is this host right now, and is anything actually stalling?

UptimeSeconds.sentence: Seconds since boot, whole. A counter: it only advances, and two correct readings differ by the time between them.

BootedAt.sentence: The boot moment, derived as now minus uptime — a constant of the boot computed against a moving clock, so two correct readings jitter by a second and it is declared as the gauge that makes that honest.

LoadAvg1.sentence: The kernel's one-minute load average: runnable plus uninterruptible tasks, decaying.

CpuCount.sentence: Logical CPUs available to this host, the denominator LoadPerCpu1 is judged against.

LoadPerCpu1.sentence: LoadAvg1 divided by CpuCount, two decimals: the number that makes load comparable across hosts of different widths.

MemAvailableBytes.sentence: What the kernel estimates it could reclaim without swapping — the honest headroom figure, not free.

MemUsedPercent.sentence: MemUsedBytes over MemTotalBytes, rounded. On a ZFS host this counts the ARC as used; the adjusted figure beside it is what the memory rules judge.

MemUsedPercentAdjusted.sentence: Memory used OUTSIDE the ZFS ARC, as a share of total: the ARC counts as used yet shrinks under demand, so a cache-warm ZFS host reads nearly full while under no pressure at all. Equal to MemUsedPercent where there is no ARC. This is the number the memory rules fire on — derived here so the judgement can be data rather than arithmetic (DESIGN 17).

SwapUsedPercent.sentence: Swap used over swap total, rounded. Absent on a swapless host: no swap means no swap pressure to be innocent of, and 0% would claim otherwise.

ArcSizeBytes.sentence: The ZFS ARC's current size. Absent without the zfs module — absence is the fact; zero would read as an empty cache.

ArcTargetBytes.sentence: The size the ARC is currently aiming for (arcstats c).

CpuTimes.sentence: Cumulative CPU time per state since boot, USER_HZ ticks, in the kernel's own field names. Counters, not a percentage: this collector holds no previous sample, so a client derives utilisation across the window it actually observed. Iowait is the member worth reading alone — a host can be 90% busy doing nothing but waiting for a disk.

NetCounters.sentence: Per-interface cumulative RX/TX bytes since boot. Counters, never rates, for the same no-previous-sample reason.

DiskCounters.sentence: Per-whole-device cumulative read/write bytes plus IoTicksMs and WeightedIoMs — the pair that separates a saturated device from a merely busy one, which bytes per second cannot.

PsiCpuSomeAvg10.sentence: The kernel's decaying 10-second share of wall time in which at least one task was waiting on cpu. Absent without CONFIG_PSI, never zero.

PsiCpuSomeAvg60.sentence: The kernel's decaying 60-second share of wall time in which at least one task was waiting on cpu. Absent without CONFIG_PSI, never zero.

PsiCpuSomeAvg300.sentence: The kernel's decaying 300-second share of wall time in which at least one task was waiting on cpu. Absent without CONFIG_PSI, never zero.

PsiMemorySomeAvg10.sentence: The kernel's decaying 10-second share of wall time in which at least one task was waiting on memory. Absent without CONFIG_PSI, never zero.

PsiMemorySomeAvg60.sentence: The kernel's decaying 60-second share of wall time in which at least one task was waiting on memory. Absent without CONFIG_PSI, never zero.

PsiMemorySomeAvg300.sentence: The kernel's decaying 300-second share of wall time in which at least one task was waiting on memory. Absent without CONFIG_PSI, never zero.

PsiMemoryFullAvg10.sentence: The kernel's decaying 10-second share of wall time in which every task with work to do was stalled on memory. Absent without CONFIG_PSI, never zero.

PsiMemoryFullAvg60.sentence: The kernel's decaying 60-second share of wall time in which every task with work to do was stalled on memory. Absent without CONFIG_PSI, never zero.

PsiMemoryFullAvg300.sentence: The kernel's decaying 300-second share of wall time in which every task with work to do was stalled on memory. Absent without CONFIG_PSI, never zero.

PsiIoSomeAvg10.sentence: The kernel's decaying 10-second share of wall time in which at least one task was waiting on io. Absent without CONFIG_PSI, never zero.

PsiIoSomeAvg60.sentence: The kernel's decaying 60-second share of wall time in which at least one task was waiting on io. Absent without CONFIG_PSI, never zero.

PsiIoSomeAvg300.sentence: The kernel's decaying 300-second share of wall time in which at least one task was waiting on io. Absent without CONFIG_PSI, never zero.

PsiIoFullAvg10.sentence: The kernel's decaying 10-second share of wall time in which every task with work to do was stalled on io. Absent without CONFIG_PSI, never zero.

rules.sentence: Memory outside the ZFS ARC is nearly exhausted; MemAvailable (what the kernel could reclaim without swapping) is almost gone.
Memory outside the ZFS ARC is running low.
Memory reads nearly full, but most of it is the ZFS ARC — the cache yields under demand, so this is occupancy, not pressure.
Swap is heavily used; memory demand has exceeded RAM.
This host made no progress for a fifth of the last minute: every task that had work to do was waiting on memory reclaim (thrashing).
Every task that had work to do was waiting on memory reclaim for part of the last minute. Tasks with nothing to do are not counted.
At least one task was waiting for CPU for most of the last minute — some, not full: a weaker claim than the memory and I/O stalls, worded so identical-looking percentages cannot be read as one thing.
This host made no progress for a fifth of the last minute: every task that had work to do was waiting on I/O. Tasks with nothing to do are not counted.

collections.redaction_exemption: every fact is a number, a timestamp, or a counter map keyed by interface and device names; on the payloads this collector reads those names are kernel-assigned identifiers, and no free-form document is served as evidence
